about: The gospel of the Third Sunday of Advent. The delegation from Jerusalem asks three times, and John's answers grow shorter each time: I am not the Christ, I am not, no. Only after that does he say who he is, and he says it in Isaias' words. The Bethania of the last sentence lies beyond the Jordan and is not the one near Jerusalem where Martha and Mary lived.

seg.tr: At that time the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to John to ask him:
He confessed and did not deny, but confessed: I am not the Christ.

fn.w021: With “conféssus” (w020) this forms the perfect of a deponent verb. English builds the same tense with an auxiliary, which this cell supplies.
fn.w027: The same compound perfect as at the first “conféssus”, repeated.
fn.w028: It opens direct speech rather than a subordinate clause. The Greek puts “hoti” before the quotation and the Latin renders it word for word. The translation drops it, because English opens a quotation with the colon alone.

seg.tr: They asked him: What then? Are you Elijah?
He said: I am not. Are you the prophet? He answered: No.

fn.w045: Latin has no article, so by itself it cannot say whether they ask about a prophet or about the Prophet promised to Moses. The Greek behind it has the definite article, and this edition reads it so — the gloss says the prophet.

seg.tr: They said therefore to him: Who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say of yourself?
He said: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: Make straight the way of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said.

fn.w071: A genitive participle used as a noun: “of one who is crying”.

seg.tr: Those who had been sent were Pharisees.

fn.w084: A pluperfect passive built on “fúerant” rather than on “erant”.

seg.tr: They asked him: Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?
John answered them: I baptize in water; but among you stands One whom you do not know.

fn.w114: A predicate adjective with “stetit”, governing the partitive genitive “vestrum” (w116).
fn.w116: The partitive genitive of “vos”, not the possessive “vester”.

seg.tr: He is the One who is to come after me, who has precedence over me. I am not worthy to loosen the strap of His sandal.

fn.w140: It repeats what “cuius” (w133) has already said. The doubled pointer follows Hebrew syntax.

seg.tr: These things were done in Bethania beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
